findings.issue: 'The bear case is now consensus' has no supporting headline, and the Wolfe/Peller CNBC item carries a day-granular 1 Feb stamp that may precede PayPal's results.
findings.resolution: Replaced with a neutral 'credible counterweight' framing attributed to Wolfe Research via n0482; no consensus claim.

findings.issue: 'nothing like the Fed's path is priced' is not in any own-date headline or card field.
findings.resolution: Replaced with 'an eventual rather than imminent move', which is what n1424's headline ('eventual rate hike') supports.

findings.issue: Attributed the 'NATO enlargement to Poland was a fraud' quote to Putin alone; the headline (n1569) names only a Putin-Orban press conference.
findings.resolution: Reworded to a Putin-Orban press conference where enlargement is called a fraud.

findings.issue: Causal claims beyond the headlines: the Gulf Times item (n0114) was presented as the explanation for the 10Y lagging the 2Y, and the DXY drop was asserted to be caused by hawkish ECB/BoE signals.
findings.resolution: Softened to 'may help explain' and 'consistent with'.

findings.issue: Spotify listed as punished (n0592, 2 Feb) although the card shows +9.18% on Friday and +0.84% over five sessions.
findings.resolution: Added 'before a +9.18% bounce on Friday' with the card source tag.

findings.issue: All card figures (instrument, session, 1/5/20-session horizon, units), curve wording (bear flattening, moderately steep), prior-close tags (crypto 2022-02-06, Shanghai 2022-01-28) and Meta Platforms (FB) naming checked against the 2022-02-07 card; no cross-date contamination (no 2022-01-31 or 2022-02-10 values) found.

All 252 cited IDs are stamped before cutoff. Day-granular items n0145 (Caixin PMI, 29 Jan stamp), n2147 (Sunday tipswatch), n1502/n1280 (weekend) describe pre-cutoff events or pending items only. Caixin services PMI and Monday Asian trading are not described as outcomes; Macron mission and Polish MPC treated as pending.

Stances and Playbooks (banks over industrials, offshore over onshore China, energy and quality over long-duration growth) are consistent across sections. No input narration, no 'META'/'DJT'/'XYZ' tickers, no numeric spot-FX, no invasion stated as fact.

scope_limits: Reviewed only the 2022-02-07 feed headlines (titles/src/stamps, not article bodies), card, exclusions and BRIEF; no other date, retail draft, or web access. Judgements on day-granular stamps rely on headline meaning only. Interpretive trade-view statements (e.g. causal market commentary) were accepted when they are modal and consistent with cited headlines.

recommended_exclusions.reason: RBA 'Minutes of the Monetary Policy Meeting' of 1 February are published two weeks after the meeting; the 1 Feb stamp is misdated and the content is after cutoff.
'BoE raises rates by most since 1995 even as long recession looms' does not match the 3 Feb 25 bp hike; it describes a later, larger decision (misdated/anachronistic).
'Bitcoin Price Predictions for 2025' is a later-dated page with a stale 1 Feb stamp.
'A List of Fake Crypto Websites & Trading Platforms 2023' references a later year; misdated.
Sunday-stamped CNBC 'Dollar up, euro down as pair face off' conflicts with the card's -1.84% five-session DXY move and may describe Monday trading after cutoff.

exclusion_rebinds.reason: Root added editorial exclusions for uncited records after review; reviewed component content unchanged.
